newsitem.title: UK: Global gas output to rise 40 pct by 2005 - report.
newsitem.headline: Global gas output to rise 40 pct by 2005 - report.

text.p: World natural gas production will rise to 315.667 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) (3,226.12 billion cubic metres per year) by 2005, up by 40 percent from 225.318 mmcfd (2,302.75 bcm per year) last year, Geneva-based Petroconsultants said on Monday.

Announcing the publication of its Worldwide Natural Gas 10-Year Production Forecast, Petroconsultants said demand among producing nations will continue to grow at an average annual rate of 3.4 percent between 1996 and 2005.
Gas exports will rise by 84 percent by 2005 as global gas trade surges and regionalism diminishes.
Offshore gas output will grow, but will constitute only 27 percent of global supply by 2005, the report said.

The report forecasts that all regions will end the period at new production highs, presently depressed production in the former Soviet Union will resurge strongly, and very few major producers will enter long-term decline.
The exception to this is the Netherlands, so that by 2005 the largest producers will include all today's leaders less the Netherlands.
